messages.subject: Possible bug in facet_wrap
parts:
Hi all,

I'm trying to generate a plot that shows the physical distribution of laboratory failures across a series of laboratory plates.  I'm sure there are better ways of doing this, but I'm taking my full dataset, subsetting the failed assays, and trying to plot counts of failures by plate and plate column (in this example):

data = read.csv("sample_data.txt",sep="\t",header=T)
failed = subset(data, NONEMPTY_MISSING_RATE>0.03)

pdf("bug.pdf")

p = ggplot(failed,aes(x=factor(PLATE),y=factor(DNA_COL))) +
    stat_bin2d(aes(size=..count..,color=..count..),geom="point",binwidth=c(1,1)) +
    opts(axis.text.x=theme_text(angle=-90, hjust=0, size=0.5)) +
    facet_wrap( ~ GROUP, scales="free_x")

p

dev.off()

This works for some datasets, but has started to fail with the following error message:

Error in cut.default(data$x, sort(breaks$x), include.lowest = TRUE) :
  invalid number of intervals
Calls: print ... FUN -> <Anonymous> -> <Anonymous> -> cut -> cut.default
Execution halted


This error goes away if I remove the 'scales="free_x"', which suggests this may be a bug.  I'm happy to share the raw data, since it is scrubbed of all sensitive attributes.

Best regards,
-Kevin Jacobs

It's a bug, or at least a corner case, but not in facet_wrap. Here is
a more minimal example that gives the same error, but without
faceting:

minimal <-
structure(list(PLATE = structure(1L, .Label = "PB14298", class =
"factor"),
DNA_COL = structure(1L, .Label = "10", class =
"factor")),
.Names = c("PLATE", "DNA_COL"), class = "data.frame")

ggplot(minimal, aes(x=PLATE, y=DNA_COL)) + stat_bin2d(binwidth=c(1,1))

The problem is that there is only 1 unique combination of x and y, and
when stat_bin2d goes to create the bins to aggregate into, a corner
case happens. This happened in your example in panel 4 (GROUP4) where
in your data, there was only one one PLATE (PB14298) and one DNA_COL
("10"). When you didn't have free x-axes, it didn't happen because
the entire range of plates were on all graphs. Actually, the fact
that PLATE and DNA_COL are factors is not a requirement to see this
behavior:

minimal2 <-
structure(list(PLATE = 1, DNA_COL = 1),
.Names = c("PLATE", "DNA_COL"),
row.names = 1L,
class = "data.frame")

ggplot(minimal2, aes(x=PLATE, y=DNA_COL)) +
stat_bin2d(binwidth=c(1,1))

Details as to what causes the bug:

The problem is that, in the calculate method (? not sure of the S4
terminology) of StatBin2d, line 55 ends up making a call to cut which
boils down to:

cut(c(1,1), 1, include.lowest=TRUE) #This by itself gives the ultimate
error message seen

the first argument is the range of the x variable; the second is the
result of the fullseq call at line 40. There, rather than getting a
vector of breakpoints, you get a single number (1). The second
argument to cut should be either a vector of length 2 or more which
are the breakpoints, or a single number greater than or equal to 2
which is the number of breakpoints. Here, it is neither; it is a
single number equal to 1. The fact that factors were used made it
more likely that you would get 1 as the one and only value. In fact,
with a continuous value other than 1, it works (in so much as it does
not throw an error), but may not actually be doing what you think:

minimal3 <-
structure(list(PLATE = 3, DNA_COL = 3),
.Names = c("PLATE", "DNA_COL"),
row.names = 1L,
class = "data.frame")
ggplot(minimal3, aes(x=PLATE, y=DNA_COL)) +
stat_bin2d(binwidth=c(1,1))

fullseq(c(3,3), 1)
# [1] 3
cut(c(3,3),3)
# [1] (2.999,3.001] (2.999,3.001]
# Levels: (2.997,2.999] (2.999,3.001] (3.001,3.003]

So to trigger it, all the x values must be 1, and the binwidth must
also be 1 (otherwise fullseq will give more than one value or a value
other than 1).

Workaround:
If the binwidth is not exactly 1, then there isn't a problem, so the
binwidth can be set to c(1.0000000001, 1) which will give the same
effective results until the corner case is fixed.

Unrelated:

In stat-bin2d.r, line 45, should the third argument to seq be
binwidth[1] instead of binwidth[2]?

--Brian Diggs

Thanks for digging into this problem! I think the underlying problem
is that currently, fullseq(c(1, 1), 1) returns 1. I'm completely sure
what it should return, however:

* c(0, 1)
* c(0.5, 1.5)
* c(1, 2)
* c(-Inf, Inf)

I'm currently leaning towards the second option.
